literal: "The ruler is a cruel man" saying-that which-is-spoken painful word king, lifespan having-hastened swiftly will-perish.
translation: A king who draws the painful words "Our ruler is cruel" will see his lifespan rapidly shrink and will swiftly perish.
modern: நம் அரசன் கொடுமையானவன் என்று மக்களால் சொல்லப்படும் துன்பமான சொற்களைப் பெறும் அரசன், தன் ஆயுள் குறைந்து விரைவில் அழிவான்.
explanation: This couplet warns against ruling by terror and oppression. If a king's actions cause his people to speak the painful words 'Our ruler is cruel,' he brings about his own downfall. The word 'uṟai' has multiple meanings including dwelling, drop, and lifespan; here, lifespan or duration of rule fits best, as it 'hastens' (kaṭuki) to an end, meaning his time in power and life will swiftly perish.
